etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French récipient, from Latin recipiēns, present participle of recipiō (“to receive”).

quote.citation: 2023 March 8, Howard Johnston, “Was Marples the real railway wrecker?”, in RAIL, number 978, page 52:
quote.text: And it [bribery and fraud] didn't stop there. Both Sir Winston Churchill and later Labour leader Michael Foot were allegedly regular recipients of private cheques that would have seen them summarily sacked in this present age of transparency.

definitions.definition: (medicine) A person receiving donor organs or tissues.
(chemistry) The portion of an alembic or other still in which the distilled liquid is collected.
